notes: Record type: Observatory for a single citizen-science RadioJOVE participant station (Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory, Industry, Pennsylvania), operating since 2013, still active. This is not a professional spacecraft/observatory with instrument PIs and description papers; the five 'instruments' are amateur-built antenna+receiver systems, all operated by one person (Jim Brown), none with a scholarly description paper. Authorship evidence is therefore intrinsically thin.

STRONGEST REVIEWER DECISION: James (Jim) Brown is the de facto operator/founder of HNRAO — DataProducer of every HNRAO data product, sole TechnicalContact across the Observatory and all five Instrument records, and his SMWG Person organization literally is HNRAO. Per the skill's role gate he is formally EXCLUDED (all his roles — TechnicalContact, DataProducer — are non-qualifying), so he is recorded as excluded rather than promoted on the automated pass. He is the single most likely true station-level author and the top candidate for the human reviewer to promote. No qualifying-role, publication, or provider-PI evidence was found to elevate him automatically: the SUG provider page is defunct and the HNRAO personal site (hnrao.weebly.com) does not print an author byline.

No CMAD (not applicable to a citizen-science project) and no Strong-tier evidence of any kind (no HNRAO-specific overview paper, no CMAD front page, no provider PI page). The only included candidate is the RadioJOVE project PI via the parent ObservatoryGroup record.

Scoping of James R. Thieman (included, Medium): he is PrincipalInvestigator on the parent RadioJOVE ObservatoryGroup record (spase://SMWG/Observatory/RadioJOVE) and a RadioJOVE co-founder — the project-level PI of the umbrella project, treated here like a mission PI reached by following the group link upward. REVIEWER: decide whether project-level leadership belongs on an individual participant-station record, or only on the RadioJOVE group record. RadioJOVE has dozens of participant stations; Thieman is not HNRAO-specific.

Project-level founders/leaders (Chuck Higgins, Leonard N. Garcia) are recorded as excluded with a scoping reason: they are RadioJOVE project-scope, not authors of this specific participant station, and hold no qualifying role on any HNRAO-linked record. They are properly candidates for the RadioJOVE ObservatoryGroup record, not HNRAO.

No description-paper selection was performed for the instruments: none of the five amateur-built systems has a scholarly description paper, so no position-based (Strong/Medium) author evidence exists. Each instrument is logged in pending_instrument_runs with reason 'paper not located'. There is a RadioJOVE PROJECT overview literature (e.g. 'The Radio Jove Project: Citizen science for radio astronomy', doi:10.1553/pre8s125; book chapter 'The NASA Radio Jove Project', doi:10.1007/978-3-030-54906-0_12) but these describe the parent project/group, not the HNRAO station, so their author lists were not harvested onto this station-level record (wrong-level paper, analogous to using a mission-overview paper for a single instrument).

Instrument coverage: reverse lookup via github.com/hpde/SMWG (Instrument/Ground/HNRAO) found all five instrument records; all ObservatoryIDs confirm HNRAO. External roster from the record's own Description matches the five records; the Mosely 20 MHz Yagi antenna is named in the Description but unregistered (no Instrument record, no data product) — surfaced in instrument_coverage.missing_from_spase for curators, not pursued as it produces no archived data.

The RadioJOVE Spectrograph Users Group provider page (http://radiojove.org/SUG/) is defunct — the radiojove.org domain now serves unrelated spam/e-commerce content. Provider-team corroboration (which might have named Jim Brown as station operator with a clearer descriptor) was therefore unavailable. The live NASA project site is https://radiojove.gsfc.nasa.gov/.
